utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. All the accused are here. And Defence teams, only Ms. Condon is absent. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls. We are coming back to you on a matter raised yesterday during the sitting by Madam Fauveau, with whom -- or with whose submission the Defence team for Mr. Nikolic and also for Colonel Beara associated themselves. Essentially the request, as you will recall, is that we issue an injunction against -- or to the Prosecution not to proof Ms. Frease. After that the Defence submissions on intercepts to which our 17 January decision relates, has been filed. As I told you yesterday, we proceeded with our discussions on the matter at length this morning, and we are now giving you, or giving you our decision on the matter. To begin with, it is important to stress, and this has been stressed throughout all the debate that has been going on, but we stress it once more, that what we have before us is a legal issue as to whether certain evidence is admissable in these proceedings. There is no question that the party proffering evidence carries the onus to establish its relevance, authenticity and probative value. We assume that is the reason for the extensive evidence adduced by the Prosecution on these intercepts to date. At the same time, the Defence has brought a positive challenge to this evidence that appears to go beyond a simple attack on the Prosecution evidence. We would like to have some idea of what that objection is based upon. We reiterate once more that what we are asking the Defence to provide is a brief outline which details the basis upon which the objection to the admissibility of evidence is premised. As Judge Kwon lucidly pointed out, or described it yesterday, what we are seeking is the crux of why you say this evidence should not be allowed. We do not expect the Defence to set out the specific examples from the evidence that support those arguments or point to particular intercepts at this time. Rather, we need to know whether the Defence are basing their arguments on reliability, continuity, authenticity, forgery, et cetera. The statement from counsel to Mr. Nikolic yesterday that the issue is solely one of reliability, perhaps supported by some very general examples, is an illustration, is an example of what we are looking for in this filing. Further, we want to have this information before us, as we have had occasion to point earlier, prior to the testimony of Ms. Frease as it will assist us in her overarching evidence in relation to potential arguments to be advanced. Now, the suggestion has been made that these goals can be met through an ex parte filing, which would inform the Chamber of the nature of these arguments without giving -- without passing on that information to the Prosecution. Alternatively it is argued that after this information is disclosed the Prosecution should be prohibited from proofing or speaking to Ms. Frease about her evidence. We fail to understand how this will assist the Trial Chamber in its goal to have evidence relevant to the issues at hand adduced before it. If the Prosecution is aware very generally of the areas in contention, then the evidence adduced will be responsive to those issues and will assist the Trial Chamber in reference to the legal question before it. This is particularly the case with a witness such as Stefanie Frease who had no involvement in the original generation of this material and who will testify to matters of continuity and process. Further, if, as counsel suggested yesterday, the Prosecution is already aware of the basis of the objection, then there can be no harm whatsoever in providing that information at this stage. We have already made it clear that witnesses must be confronted with matters in issue pertinent to their testimony. Further, we can assure you that we are not prepared to decide this important issue without having the relevant evidence before us. In the light of those facts, the only effect the approach suggested by the Defence would have is to delay the timing of the presentation of the evidence from direct examination to re-examination, examination by Chamber or, in the extreme, the need to recall witnesses. We are not convinced as to the benefit of such an approach to either of the parties and to the Trial Chamber. For this reason we are not prepared to vary our decision and provide for an ex parte filing. Nor are we going -- or intend to prohibit the Prosecution from speaking to Ms. Frease after the information to which the 17 January decision refers is disclosed. All right. Any other preliminaries that you would like to raise before the witness is shown in? Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Simply to say that we take good note of that decision and we, on behalf of Drago Nikolic, we apologise, it stems from a misunderstanding of the Trial Chamber's order, for which we are responsible, and given the nature of the filing that is requested by the Chamber, we have absolutely no problem in obeying the Trial Chamber's order. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can assure you, although I haven't -- I am not consulting my clients [sic] on this that we are very appreciative of that statement, Mr. Bourgon. Madam Fauveau, would you like to associate yourself with Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I was sure of that.

utterances.speaker: THE FRENCH INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear, Madam Fauveau, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So any further -- we didn't hear Madam Fauveau. Madam Fauveau said certainly she associates herself with the statement of Mr. Bourgon. I should be paid extra for interpretation. So any further preliminary issues? None. Curtains down, please. As we did in the case of the previous witness, the very first thing that the Trial Chamber will do is to give what my country would call caution to -- to the witness. All right. I also wanted to advise you that the last session of today's sitting we will be invoking Rule 15 bis. Unfortunately I need to leave the Tribunal somewhat early today because of a personal -- pre-arranged personal commitment that I couldn't change. And Judge Prost will preside instead of me -- Judge Kwon will preside instead of me and proceed pursuant to Rule 15 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Welcome to this Tribunal. You are about to start your evidence. Before you do so, our -- Madam Usher is going to hand you the text of a solemn declaration that you are required to make under our rules. Please read it out aloud and that will be your commitment with us that you will be testifying the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a seat and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Two things before you start giving evidence. One is that the Prosecution has requested and we granted protective measures for you, being the use of a pseudonym instead of your name and also face and voice distortion. I trust this has already been explained to you. I only want a confirmation from you that this is to your satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. The other thing is this: One of our rules provides that a witness may object to answer a question or to make a statement which might tend to incriminate him. Objection, however, or the right to object, does not necessarily mean that you will be exempted from answering questions that are put to you, which -- in answering might incriminate you. That lies within the discretion of the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber will weigh everything and decide whether you should answer such questions or not. However, if you are compelled by the Trial Chamber to answer such questions or to make such statements, then testimony evidence compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in any subsequent prosecution that might be taken against you, except if we catch you perjuring yourself, if we catch you giving false testimony. In that case, what you have stated can be made use of in subsequent proceedings for false testimony, but only in that case. Otherwise, anything you say here, if you are compelled to say it, will not be able to be used in your regard in any proceedings that might be taken against you. I trust this has already been explained to you to an extent. I just want confirmation from you that you understand the import of my explanation to you and that you do not require any further explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this has already been explained to me and I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Nicholls will go first, and then he will be followed by cross-examination from the various Defence teams. Mr. Nicholls, may I please remind everyone to switch off one's microphone once the witness is testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If could I have the assistance of the usher. The usher is handing you now a sheet of paper. I want you to read it silently to yourself, not out loud and just confirm yes or no, is your name printed on that sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That will be P02405 under seal when we come to tender it, if it could be shown to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know whether the information that we have should be corrected or whether what's in the transcript should be corrected, but according to the sheet referring to Prosecution exhibits the pseudonym sheet is marked at P02404, while in the transcript we have P02405, as rightly pointed out by Judge Kwon. 2405, all right. So we don't need to correct the transcript, we need to correct -- yes, okay. Thank you, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you some questions about the time period after the fall of Srebrenica. Do you recall when the fall of Srebrenica was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I remember that it was in the summer of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall the exact date? If you do --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, after that event, were you ordered to guard any prisoners, Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you some questions about that now. Where did you first guard prisoners after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That was in Orahovac at the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you could describe in your own words to me, please, how did you come to perform that guard duty in Orahovac at the school building? Who told you where you were going to go? What time of day was it? Just describe to me what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Well, it was evening, I was on duty at the gate in the standard barracks, when I was ordered to go to Orahovac because prisoners from Srebrenica were arriving and they needed to be guarded. It was evening; I wouldn't be able to say exactly what time. I was ordered by some officer whose name I don't know right now. It was either Drago Nikolic (redacted) (redacted), because in those days I received orders only from the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we know exactly why. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into open session. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, other than that these prisoners were from Srebrenica, the ones being taken to the Orahovac school, were you told anything else about these prisoners or given any other advice about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you tell me what that was, please? What were you told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That we had to be very careful because those were dangerous soldiers who were ready to do anything. That is to say, to pull in a guard into the crowd and kill him there, something similar had happened in Bratunac previously and we were told that we had to be extra careful when guarding those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, how were you transported, if you remember, to Orahovac? How did you go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember how many of your fellow military -- members from the military police went with you to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say that either. There were not too many of us, perhaps a section or two at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how many is a section, if you could just explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: A section or a squad has six to seven men in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could have in e-court 1692 on the screen, please. And in a moment, sir, there will be a picture appearing hopefully on the computer screen in front of you. Take a look at it when it comes up and then I'll ask you a question. Do you have a picture of a building in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I showed you this picture in my office the other day, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell me where this place is, this building that we see in the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It's the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We just wanted to make sure that we have the e-court reference of the photo. We do have it in the transcript. Thank you, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the school was it daylight or was it dark? Can you tell me what -- about how late it was, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time, but I think it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you tell me who else was at the school there? Who -- which people did you see when you arrived at the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: There were some soldiers besides the prisoners who were already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you tell which unit or units these soldiers belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really couldn't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Approximately how many soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really wouldn't know the exact answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were these soldiers doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: They were standing in front of the area in front of the school, just moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to be very clear when we're talking about soldiers here, are we talking about VRS soldiers or Muslim soldiers that you are talking about in front of the school standing around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What was happening, what was physically happening with the prisoners when you arrived at the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Nothing was happening. They were going in quietly from the bus into the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How many buses did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but there were more than two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether these buses were military buses or whether they had civilian markings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that they were civilian buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether there had been any escort for these buses which brought the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any escort at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how long did the buses stay there? Were you able to see the buses leave at any point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I could see that as soon as a bus was empty it would leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if you can give us an estimate how many prisoners do you think when you arrived that evening were being brought into the gym of the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really couldn't give you even an estimate. The gym was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you saw Drago Nikolic at the Orahovac school that evening, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: They assigned us to the places where we would be spending the night and guarding those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And specifically who was assigning you -- who was -- you can say the name. Who was telling you where to go and where to spend the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Drago Nikolic, specifically he assigned us to the places where we would be spending that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you say "we," "Drago Nikolic told us," or "we," who was the "we" you were referring to? Who was Drago Nikolic issuing these assignments to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: To us, the military policemen who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what specifically were your orders from Drago Nikolic that night, the ones given to you personally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we need to stay -- we are in open session, all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personal order that I and my colleague, whoever happened to be there, should be assigned to a particular place. We were ordered to stay in a certain place and spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we've seen the picture of the school, and I know you did a diagram before, but can you just describe where was your place at the school? Where did you -- where were you posted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I was put behind the school. I cannot explain exactly. I didn't spend the whole time there, there was some moving around the school and standing in a different place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions now about that night of guard duty. Did you see any mistreatment of any of the prisoners in the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to see if the prisoners were given any food or any water during that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I was able to see about the water, but I don't know whether this happened during the night or the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That doesn't explain much. Perhaps you can pursue the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Whether it was that night when you were on guard duty or the next day, what happened? Do you recall if the prisoners were brought some water or given some water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay awake that night on guard duty? Was it the whole night, part of the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that I stayed awake the whole night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to get any sleep while you were at the Orahovac school doing this guard duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you describe that just a little bit, how long you were able to sleep and where you slept, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The next day, during the day, I slept for a while on the grass behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you some questions about that next day. What happened in the morning when the sun came up at the school in Orahovac, if you can describe to us how that day began and what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Nothing particular happened in the morning. Everything was the same. This was during the morning, we continued to guard the prisoners who were in the gym and there were no other things happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, do you remember any more prisoners arrived during the day-time that next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't think so, during the time that I was there awake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, besides you and your fellow MPs from the Zvornik Brigade, do you know -- were you able to tell which other VRS soldiers, if any, were present around the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes. There were other soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe the civilians? Who were they and -- if you could tell, and how were they behaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: There were women and children. That's who the civilians were. The others were all in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And approximately, if you can, how many soldiers were there other than you and your fellow Zvornik Brigade military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really couldn't say. There were more, maybe a company, 50 or more soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to tell which unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sure. Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, this tall officer of the army of Republika Srpska, whose name you don't know, were you able to tell what unit or what rank he might have had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wasn't able to notice that he wasn't from the Zvornik Brigade. There was no such insignia, and I knew all the officers from the Zvornik Brigade anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, other than that he was tall, as best you can, can you describe this other VRS officer not from the Zvornik Brigade who we're talking about? Best you can recall, what he looked like and what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: He was wearing a uniform of the army of Republika Srpska, he was older, with grey hair and with glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was this officer doing, the one you have just described with grey hair and glasses, when you saw him at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Nothing special, other than speaking with Mr. Nikolic. I didn't really see him do anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Nicholls. In relation to this tall officer of the army of Republika Srpska, the witness, although not being in a position to tell us which unit or what rank he might have had, he comes to the conclusion that he wasn't from the Zvornik Brigade because he carried no such insignia, and in addition he adds, "I knew all the officers from the Zvornik Brigade anyway." Now, previously in his testimony he has referred to soldiers, and when asked by you if he could tell us which unit they came from, he couldn't. So my question to him is the following: On the basis of what he has just stated, recognising all the members of the Zvornik Brigade and insignia of the Zvornik Brigade, can he categorically exclude that any of the soldiers he saw at the Orahovac school the first day and the second day, can he exclude categorically that they could have been from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think you heard His Honour's question, sir. Are you able to say that all these other VRS soldiers you saw were not from the Zvornik Brigade, based on the insignia, or are you -- can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I didn't know all the soldiers in the Zvornik Brigade. I don't know if all of them were from our brigade. As for the officers, I knew them because I worked at the barracks for over three years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your witness, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, the tall officer with the grey hair and glasses, can you tell approximately what time of the day it was that you saw him at the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know what the exact time of the day was, but I saw him during the day. It wasn't early in the day, but sometime during the day. Not early, maybe in the afternoon sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how often did you see him during the day at this school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: He stayed there for a while and I was able to see him from the place where I was at that time, maybe two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when Drago Nikolic was talking to this officer, where were they standing, say in relationship -- in relation to the front of the school where there is the playground and the road? If you know, can you describe where they were standing when they were talking together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think I saw them talking on the road the first time, close to the playing field.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you see them talking any other time in any other place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. I really couldn't be quite sure about that. I couldn't be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: While Drago Nikolic and this other officer you have described were talking, what was happening with the prisoners in the school at that time? Were they in the school? Were they coming and going out? What was going on with the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that they were in the school when I saw them the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about how the prisoners came to leave the school, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you can describe that process, what you saw when the prisoners left the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The trucks came to the area in front of the school, and the prisoners then began to be boarded on to the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What kind of trucks were these? Can you describe them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that they were small military trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how were the prisoners physically -- how were they boarded on to these trucks, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: They were boarding them, we were escorting them, things were proceeding quite normally, but their -- their hands were tied behind their back, but they were going in quietly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, once a truck was full with prisoners, which direction would it leave when it left the Orahovac school that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know the exact place. It was the opposite direction from Zvornik, the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So leaving the school, pulling out, would they turn left or right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was there any escort for these trucks as they left the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really couldn't say. I was there near the trucks, or by the trucks as the prisoners were going in, but it was a -- a kind of country road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did the trucks return after they had left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were they full or -- with the prisoners, still, or empty when they returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: They would be returning empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And during this time when the trucks are leaving full of prisoners and returning empty, during that period did you see Drago Nikolic leave the school at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The whole time while Drago Nikolic was there he was moving around in different directions. I -- I think at that time he was also moving around, but I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in a vehicle on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: He would get in the car and it would drive off, so I would just see him for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In which direction would he drive off in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: In the direction that the trucks were moving. He would be going in that direction with the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe the car, please, that he was -- that you saw him in that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know what the car model was, but it was a military car, a military station wagon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that it was a metallic grey, some metallic colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, during this time that the trucks are leaving full of prisoners, coming back empty, what could you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: As I already said in my statement, I heard shooting in the direction that the trucks were going to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you describe the shooting a little bit? I know this is not a pleasant thing to talk about, what -- if you can describe what you heard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I could hear bursts of fire in the distance, like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How long did this process last? The prisoners being taken away, hearing gun-fire, trucks coming back empty, how long did that last during the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time. I think that it lasted into the night, until the gym was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Tell me how you personally came to leave the school, where you went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Pursuant to the order, I went back to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Go into private session for one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions now about what happened the next day, if you can describe what your duties were the following day after these events you have described at the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What were you told you had to do that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I was ordered to go to the school in Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember how this order was conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember it exactly. I think it was on the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where were you physically when you received that order to go to Rocevic? Where were you on duty at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I was in the standard barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Approximately, can you tell me approximately what time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It wasn't in the early morning, it was again in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were you told what your duties were going to be in Rocevic at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. We were not told anything. We were simply ordered to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And how many military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade went with you to the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say the exact number. There were a couple of us; perhaps three to five.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What happened when you got to the school in Rocevic? What did you see? What was going on there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: We came to a shop which was some 50 metres from the school. We saw some soldiers standing outside, so we didn't even go in. We stayed there for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And these soldiers you're talking about standing outside, these are VRS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And where were they standing outside? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Outside in front of the school in the Rocevic, in the yard. I wasn't able to see anything more from where I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, were you given any orders when you arrived at the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. We remained there for an hour, maybe hour and a half. We received no orders during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to see any vehicles outside the school at Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Those were small military trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was happening with those military trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: From where I stood I could only see them parked in the yard while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were you able to see whether there were any civilians, and I mean Serb civilians, in the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I wasn't able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were -- did you go into the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell whether there were any prisoners at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you describe that, please, what you saw regarding the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see the prisoners for -- from where I was standing. When the trucks started moving in front of the school, they sent us back to the barracks again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any -- any bodies anywhere around the school, any corpses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were you able to tell at all which unit or units the VRS soldiers around the school belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say exactly. I think that they were soldiers from our brigade, from one of our battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And we just need to be very clear for the transcript we are talking about, when you say "our brigade," which brigade are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And why do you -- why do you come to that conclusion that you think they were soldiers from one of the battalions of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That was my opinion. It did not even occur to me that there were soldiers from other brigades there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we're five minutes before the break. If it would be all right with the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The break is at a quarter to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm completely off, I'm sorry. In that case I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you saw these trucks moving from a distance, could you tell if there were any people being transported in the trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose that it was the same thing as what happened in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I ask you to explain that a bit? Who was being transported in the trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Prisoners from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if you -- I know you were standing a little far away, but could you give some idea of how many trucks you saw transporting prisoners away from the school in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: There were a couple of trucks leaving. I wouldn't be able to say exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you see any trucks arriving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. While I was there I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you left the school at Rocevic, what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It was before the dark. I didn't stay there long. I wouldn't be able to say exactly how long, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you left, was this process of the trucks moving, taking prisoners away, was that continuing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. I wanted to revisit the events from Orahovac. I wanted to tell you that we heard that some soldiers from your unit were tasked with preventing some people who were -- let's call them civilians, even though there were many among them who were armed, from entering the gym of the school because they wanted to settle scores with the prisoners. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you perhaps in the group who was tasked with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, do you know what is it that these people wanted? Why did they want to settle scores with these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that those were people who had some issues, who were upset or were families of soldiers who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they consider that the people in the gym were to blame for the death of their loved ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Most likely, yes, because they were enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, was their fury so great they were prepared to kill those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like now to go back to the event in Rocevic. You received an order to go with your unit to Rocevic. Tell me, please, your unit, or rather the group that went to Rocevic, was it the only one who went there, or were you split into subgroups so that some went earlier, some went later. I don't know if I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The question was clear to me but I can't tell you whether we were split into subgroups or were called there because perhaps they needed reinforcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to be more clear. Was there a group before you, a group from the same unit as you? I don't want to give the name of the unit, since we are in open session. Was there another group already in Rocevic when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know anything about any group, but I know about lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about soldiers, you can't remember seeing some soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon your arrival did another group arrive from your unit to Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say, because I can't say when I left Rocevic -- or rather whether upon leaving Rocevic I went to the barracks or home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were there can I conclude that no group of soldiers from your unit arrived while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Zivanovic. I was just going to draw your attention and also to the attention of the witness that you were going too fast. You need to allow a small, short pause between question and answer. And -- because the interpreters need to translate to us in English and French, so if you don't allow this pause, they will have problems, and they were having problems. So Mr. Meek or Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what other members of the Zvornik Brigade military police were with you or were sent to Orahovac and Rocevic School in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I think we might go into private session for that. But I wanted to put my question out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And you also need to remember to switch off your mic. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The individual that I just mentioned in private session that we will not identify him here now, but concentrating on that individual, do you know if that individual was with you in Orahovac in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can't say that for sure. That person was with me in our unit for a long time. We had various assignments together. Now, as to -- as for that specific occasion, whether he was there with me, I can't say. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether or not this individual that we are speaking of gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in March of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I am aware, I heard that the Prosecution took a statement from him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And are you also, sir, aware that this individual who gave his statement to the OTP in March of 2002, that he was considered a suspect in connection with the crimes that are alleged to have occurred at the Orahovac school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I'm not aware of him being a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell us in your capacity the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, how many times did you give them a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I gave one statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if that statement was tape-recorded in any fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware that it was tape-recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you share with us, sir, how is it that you came into contact with the Office of the Prosecutor to give a statement in connection with your duties at the Orahovac school in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just feel compelled to make the objection again that this is completely irrelevant and it's something that does not need to be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, we allowed that in the case of the previous witness, I don't see why we should disallow it in the case of this witness. So -- you didn't raise an objection then. Yes, let's proceed, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you remember the question, and if you could kind enough to give me the answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the question. I was asked by the Prosecution to come and give a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was, sir, in November of 2005, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they share with you at that time, sir, any of the testimony of the individual that we mentioned in private session that we are not going to mention in public session, about what he may have said in his statement in March of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wasn't told anything about anybody else's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long was your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2005?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: From 9.00 in the morning until 4.00 p.m., with breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So including the breaks, approximately -- what is that, six, seven hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Well, it was less than that. I had one break which was two hours long, and then one half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At this session, did the Office of the Prosecutor read you your rights and tell you that might be a suspect, given that you were a military police officer of the Zvornik Brigade at the Orahovac school in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I was told that I was summoned as a witness of an event, and I was told that I was to give a statement. Nobody mentioned anything about me being a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it then correct to assume that you were not read your rights and were not advised that you should possibly have an attorney present with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. Nobody mentioned to me anything about being a suspect or about a lawyer. As I told you, I was summon there had as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So I am correct; they didn't read you your rights and they didn't advise you, you should have a lawyer present, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. Actually, yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move to the next question, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just need to go into private session for another name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, the second individual we just identified in private session, was he a member of the military police Zvornik Brigade in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: He was a member of the Zvornik Brigade, and I think that he was a member in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about more precise than that; was he also a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recall whether Mr. -- the gentleman we identified in private session, was he at the Orahovac school with you in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if this gentleman was also at the Rocevic School in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a couple more questions before we go on the break with respect to this individual. Do you know the second individual that we just identified, do you know if he ever gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So, sir, is it fair to say that you are not aware that after you gave your statement in November, that in -- on January 18th, 2006 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- let's hear the question so that we are in a position then to decide whether to allow it or not. Go ahead and finish the question, but don't answer until we tell you to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it fair to state that you were not informed at any time by the Office of the Prosecutor then that they were going to interview this second individual six weeks after they interviewed you and they interviewed him on January 18th, 2006?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't answer that question because he already answered that when he was interviewed no one else was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go straight to the next question, but don't ask him to repeat what he has already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When was your next meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor aside from the time that you gave [microphone not activated] in November of 2005 [Realtime transcript read in error "1995"]? When is the next time that you met with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Two and a half to three months prior to that when I was informed that I would be a witness. At a trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not clear. First of all the transcript on page 18 says November of 1995. I think that is obviously a mistake. It should be 2005. Let's start from there. And secondly, you asked him when was the next time that he met with the Office of the Prosecutor. And his answer seems to indicate that he met before and not after. So more or less I think he needs to clear -- clarify that and then we have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, there is a mistake and I think I misspoke in November of 2005 I think we have established you met with the Prosecutor and I apologise for the long-winded question, but just to keep it in context, the next time you would have met with the Prosecutor or made any contact with the Office of the Prosecutor was two to three months before today, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can have the break now. It will be a 25-minute break because of the redaction. And then we will resume soon after. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are in open session. Mr. Ostojic has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, prior to the break we were discussing the fact that the Prosecutor made contact with you two or three months ago from today. And can you tell us if that contact was in person or via telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The second contact with the Prosecutor was in person, and we agreed by telephone where we would meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, where you met with the Prosecutor on this second occasion after November of 2005 when you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't see that as relevant, but if -- if the answer is going to be given, I would ask that it might be a good idea to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I need to consult my colleagues on this. Definitely if we proceed it will be in private session, but especially if a particular place is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of your question? Why is it necessary for you to know where?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We don't know -- it was just a foundational question as to where they met. I would have assumed it was via telephone, but obviously it was in person and the follow-up question was, did he give another statement at that time. I just presumed they met here. I don't know what the secrecy is if they met at another place, and I'm not interested to know if they met at a secret location, but I certainly want to know if they met and where and who was present, and if he gave another statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls, do you want to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My objection to where the place is because it's irrelevant and where we met was in an effort not to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the witness listening -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I stand on my objection. I don't need to go into that. However, I would just point out that the witness has already testified that he gave one statement in his answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is something different we are talking about here. One moment again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's proceed as follows, Mr. Ostojic. For the time being we are not convinced that there is a real need to establish the place where this second meeting took place; however, since you put it as a foundational question, I suggest that you move to your next question, the basic question. Then if it becomes obvious that we need to return to the previous foundational question, then we will reconsider our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, how long was your second meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor two or three months ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Maybe an hour. It was quite short.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were any former Zvornik Brigade military policemen in attendance at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It was just me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In November of 2005 when you gave your statement, do you know if any other military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade gave their statement at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear that a couple of them did give statements over those few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what their names are?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In private session, though; I wanted to get the question out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this individual that we just identified, sir, is he also someone that you have been in close contact with from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, it's a person who is older than I am. We do see each other, but very, very infrequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that he was a considered a suspect by the Office of the Prosecutor when he gave his statement on January 18th, 2006, six weeks after you had given yours in November of 2005? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the Office of the Prosecutor ever share with you what the testimony was of this witness? Did they tell you what he had said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to object because I think the witness said clearly, unless I'm wrong, that we -- that he was not told what other witnesses had said and about their statements. Ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that may have been with reference to the 2005 statement or to the time-frame during which that statement was -- was given. So in that respect the question is not allowed, but in respect to the subsequent meeting, maybe the question can be answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Should I restate my question, Your Honour, because I think I put, did he ever at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I draw a distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking whether I should restate it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they at any time discuss with you the testimony of this individual we identified in private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can just briefly go into private session again, Your Honour, for another name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this third individual we just identified as a member of the military police of the Zvornik Brigade, do you know if he ever gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the following individual, which I think may require us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. It's become a Yo-yo. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this individual person, a female, was she a member of the Zvornik Brigade at all in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you remember in what capacity she served in the Zvornik Brigade in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if she was present in Orahovac in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why can't you say, or why couldn't you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: These are people that I was with every day. I don't remember all the places that we were together. We spent time together every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, did naming these four individuals help refresh your recollection as to who else may have been present at the Orahovac school in July of 1995? If you do remember, don't list their names yet because, as I'm sure you've noticed, we would like to go into private session for that. Other than those four, did that help refresh your recollection of who else may have accompanied you in Orahovac in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I cannot remember these names. Maybe I can guess, but I cannot say that a certain person was with me with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, let me discuss a little bit more about your background when you first joined the military. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You were stationed there, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls, you want to go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think it would. If we're going to go through the background, it's probably wise. I don't know exactly what questions my friend will be asking, but it makes sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If he thinks for whatever cautionary reason, I'm okay with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I was precisely thinking about it. So let's redact that, and if you want to pursue the matter we'll go into private session, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would like to pursue it, if we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to the Orahovac school in which you testified on your direct here today. I think you mentioned or in your statement, at the very least, in November of 2005 that you were informed that the detainees or prisoners at the school had a tendency to kill guards. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who told you that there was this tendency to kill guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I cannot be sure. Some of my officers, some of my officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a couple of your officers here today. Were there any others other than those two officers that you have mentioned from time to time during the direct examination, are there other officers, other than those two, who may have told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. One of those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did they also, one of those two also inform you, sir, that there was a guard from Bratunac who had been killed, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, we were given that example.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you when this guard from Bratunac was killed in relation to July of 1995 and your visit to the Orahovac school or assignment, I should say, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't tell me, they just said that while guarding prisoners a guard was killed by the prisoners in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you when this happened in relation to your assignment to Orahovac school in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did they ever give you the name of the killed Bratunac guard who was -- I'm sorry, if I could restate the question. Did they ever identify the Bratunac guard who was killed by these alleged prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. We were just told the policemen guarding the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if any of the prisoners who were at the Orahovac school, were they ever checked to see if they were armed at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. Not where we were, and most likely they were searched out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now -- but you didn't see that, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I didn't see what?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you see them being searched out in the field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm interested to know what it is that you saw and observed personally. Am I correct that you did not personally witness or see any killings at Orahovac school in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, help me understand this: You had mentioned during your direct and in your statement that the guards, while at Orahovac, allowed the detainees or prisoners to go out and get some water. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How often would they have allowed that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: A couple of people would be taken from the gym, escorted by us to get water and then escorted back into the gym. I don't know how often, but a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you personally escort any of those detainees or prisoners to obtain water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, sir, given the fact that allegedly your officers told you that these prisoners had a tendency or a pre - strike that - had a tendency to kill guards, did you think it was safe for you to at that time to take these detainees or prisoners out to fetch water for them during the night or the next day while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: We were extra careful. We would take two, three, four at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Two, three, four at the most detainees, correct? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how many guards would accompany these three or four detainees or two, three or four detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Well, that depends. If there were two, they would take one. If there were four, they would take two.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now let me turn to Rocevic School for a moment. Am I also correct, sir, that you did not personally witness or see any killings at the Rocevic School in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct; no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I have your testimony proper -- properly, or understand it properly, can you tell me how many hours you spent at the Rocevic School in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Very briefly. I don't think that I spent even two hours there. Less than that, most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me, and I think I can mention this individual's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But maybe I should just go into private session, Your Honour, just so we do haven't a problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This individual, without naming his name, you mention him in your statement as well. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: He was a security officer in our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He was -- he is and was a friend of yours, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, we were neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he was one of your superior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think this part needs to be redacted. "Yes, we were neighbours."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not going to redact. Let's -- let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, this individual that we're talking about who was a friend - we'll just leave it at that - was he your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: At the time we're referring to just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So July 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long before July 1995 did you know this individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how long, but I knew him for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Without being too insistent on a precise answer, you knew him at least five years prior to 1995; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, anywhere from two to five years or if you could be precise, I'll take that. If you know exactly how much you knew him prior to 1995, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Between one year and three years, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, did you discuss with this individual the fact that were you giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2005?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was this individual, sir, present at Orahovac in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if he was present in Rocevic in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can now turn to another topic, sir. Can you tell me what you were doing in 1993 in Zvornik, being part of the Zvornik Brigade? 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes -- one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was performing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, I don't know how far the questions are going to go or how detailed but it may be necessary to go into private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I leave that in your discretion, Mr. Ostojic. --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Quickly I will identify the point and then we could go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, the location we just mentioned, I want to focus your attention in 1993 for that location. Can you tell me, were you involved at all in that location in your capacity as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I was one of the prison guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you describe for me who, sir, was at this location that you were guarding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Imprisoned soldiers and some civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall sir the ethnicities of the imprisoned soldiers and civilians that you were guarding at this location in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I remember that they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: (redacted) and we go straight into private session. You can repeat your question and he will answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't know if Mr. Bourgon or -- are going to be the last to cross-examine this witness. I suppose I -- I read it that way. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted to say that we have no cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We won't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Nor us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it came sooner than you thought, probably, Mr. Bourgon. I will be leaving in 15 minutes' time. How long are you going to cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Difficult to say at this point, Mr. President. Probably an hour, but it could be longer. It all depends on how the witness answers the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what we have agreed to do is we are going to have the break now, since, as I prepared you for it earlier on, I need to be elsewhere, unavoidably elsewhere. We will have a break now of 20 minutes. 25 minutes, yeah, redactions, 25 minutes. And then you will continue in my absence with Judge Kwon presiding. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As informed, we will be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just for the record, my name is Stephane Bourgon, I am the counsel representing Drago Nikolic in this case and accompanied with my colleagues this afternoon, and I have some questions to ask you in respect of your testimony today. I have some -- both some specific questions to ask you, and we'll begin with those specific questions, and then questions more of a general nature.
