If at all possible, if you can just confirm by a yes or a no, and if you need to say more, then by all means say so, but with the hope of saving some time, if it's possible for you to answer by a yes or a no, by all means do so. First, we'd like to go immediately into Rocevic. So you recall the events in Rocevic, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned partially. That's a good answer. I like that answer, because if I would say about your knowledge of Orahovac, you could also say that you remembered the events partially; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I would have a need to have more time about Orahovac, because I spent more time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you have a better recollection of what happened in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes. I spent more time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in respect of Rocevic, I just want to confirm to begin with that this happened the day immediately following the events in Orahovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And my question is that in Orahovac you did not see Drago Nikolic nowhere at no time during when you were at that location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I did see him at Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, my question is Rocevic, and please if we want to make this a good cross-examination and a good --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, you mentioned Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Oh. My apologies, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My apologies, Witness. I'm speaking about Rocevic, and I'm asking you to confirm that in Rocevic you did not see Drago Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That is correct. I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And with respect to the orders that you received to go to Rocevic, you mentioned at page 26, lines 24 to 25, and immediately following that, that's at page 27, lines 1 to 3, now I mention this, that's for my colleagues, that's not -- more for my colleagues than for you, so they can follow with -- my question. And the idea is that the orders to go there, you don't really remember who gave you those orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember specifically. I think it was (redacted) who sent me to Rocevic, but I cannot be 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, what you can be sure 100 per cent sure is that those orders were not given to you by Drago Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: For Rocevic, I think that that is correct. It was not issued by Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Rocevic that day, you did receive some orders, and I guess we will need to go into private session for this purpose, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will say that question over again, Witness, to ensure that this is on the record. That when you -- until the time when you heard those volley of shots, as you described, and that you saw trucks returning to the school empty, you had no idea before that, that this -- that what happened, the killing of those people, that this was about to take place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So I would say that this came to you as a complete surprise; is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Not a surprise, but I didn't know what it was all about and what would happen to the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you realised what was happening I suggest to you that you were shocked by what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can't say that I was shocked. I mean, it was a military gesture in war. It wasn't such a surprise that I was shocked, but I didn't know until that moment exactly what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So let me make my question more precise. Did you feel good about it or did you feel bad about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It didn't make me feel good. I mean what kind of a question -- must I respond to this question about my feelings?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's -- all I'm trying to get to you is that you were not happy at what was going on; so that's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you yourself, you never went to the site where those people were killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I suggest to you that you have no idea who actually fired on those people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I also suggest to you that -- that the military police of the Zvornik Brigade was not involved in those shootings and that it was limited, the role of the military police was limited to guarding the prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let's move to a bit of more general questions now. The first thing I would like to establish is your role, your specific role as a member of the military police in Orahovac. And now I refer to page 30, lines 17 to 18, where you mentioned that the role was to guard the prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in response to a question by my colleague, not the colleague across the room, but the colleague right in front of me, a question was asked of you that one of the things you had to protect the prisoners from, the civilians who were there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you yourself at the time, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in your statement when you describe that you were sent to Orahovac, you said that you were quite scared about going there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, were you impressed about the fact that you had to go to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let me ask you quite straightforward: How did you feel personally about going to Orahovac that night to guard prisoners who had just been captured? How did you feel yourself about that mission that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I always felt the same about every assignment that I was carrying out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And how was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can't explain to you how I felt when I went into combat or to guard prisoners. I mean, you can't describe it in words.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I go to your statement, I don't need to refer you, maybe that will come later. But you did say that you were warned that this could be a potentially dangerous situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Orahovac, this was -- you did refer to that in terms of the persons who were there. And you said that in addition to the military police there were some 50 soldiers who were there. Now, that's at page 18, lines 13 to 18, as well as page 12, lines 12 to 18. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Those were the page numbers of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, page number of the transcript from today. Sorry, Mr. President. If I refer to the statement, I will then refer because it is ready to be used, but if I can avoid, I will not use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You also mentioned that there were many local civilians who were there, and you also described how, I would say, mad these civilians were when you answered the question from my colleague. What I'd like to know from you is that when those civilians were there, does that -- I would suggest to you that this coincides with the time that the prisoners were put in the gym. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: There were civilians there in front throughout the time that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's what I was trying to get at, because at some point during your examination-in-chief you said that in the morning there was really nothing happening. So those civilians were always present, and that situation was always with all these people being there around you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when the -- when the actual shooting began, we've already established that you did not feel good about that, but can I describe that situation as being totally chaotic? Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know how you would describe it, but whoever happened to be there did not feel good during the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And with respect to the other soldiers who were there, because you're given a task of controlling the crowd, but there are other soldiers there and you don't know what their task is because they never relieve you from your duty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't know about other assignments. All I knew was my own, what that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But these people, these other soldiers, they were also involved with what was going on generally that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: There were many soldiers, I said that a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And those soldiers were involved into what was going on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, they were also appointed there by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I suggest to you, as you sit here today, and I'm sure that this question is not the first time you will hear a question like that, but I suggest to you that if there is one day in your life that you would like to forget, it is that day in Orahovac in July of 1995. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Well, it would be fair, but I had bad days during the war, including that day, which I would like to forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I simply suggest to you that that day in particular you would like to forget. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That day and the other bad days that I had, I would like to forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Were there many bad days like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, there were. I couldn't tell you exactly how many, but there were. The war was long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I won't get into a debate because it's not the purpose of my cross-examination, but I'm just asking that because you would like to forget this day, and this is probably the reason why there are many things that today you don't remember. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I didn't even try to remember anything about that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And today, in response to many questions that were put to you, you began your response by saying, "I think." Now, when you respond like this, just so that we are sure, and we know that, you know, for the benefit of the Court that when you say "I think," these are things that you cannot be sure of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to go over some of the details that today you seem to have some answers, but very often with the words "I think" in front of them. Just a couple of very minor examples. For example, how long you slept when you fell asleep during your guard duty. You don't remember that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the kind of vehicle that you drove in to go to Orahovac, you don't remember that either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the time that you arrived in Orahovac and the fact that it was dark or light, you are not sure of that either. That's what you answered today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'll find a reference here just to be sure that we are in the same -- that we share the same answer. And that is that at that time you mentioned that you did not know what time it was, and that you did -- you think that it was dark. Is that the right answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The evening hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, also other things that you don't -- that maybe you're not sure of is, you don't recall whether the prisoners were blindfolded or not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the kind of vehicles that were transporting those prisoners from the school to another site, you don't really remember that either, the type of vehicle and the description of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Small trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I asked you today whether these trucks are civilian or military or the exact colour, those are details you can't remember today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that they were military.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's exactly my point. You think, but you're not sure, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I can not be 100 per cent specific about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, one of the issues that I'd like to know whether you recall that, and I now refer to the transcript at page 18, lines 2 to 4. My colleague from the Prosecution suggested that maybe there was other prisoners arriving, and you mentioned in your response that could you not tell for the time that you were awake. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also responded that -- to a question from my colleague that to you the school was full, so the prisoners for you, when they arrived, they filled up the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I move in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you describe, and you've made reference to the number of hours you spent at the Orahovac school. I would just like to confirm that you must have been very hungry during that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I suggest to you that you did not eat any meals that day and you do not recall getting any meals that day, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you mean it's not correct or you did not get any meals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's not correct. So what did you eat during the period you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I got something quite meager in the course of the day. Quite unsufficient -- insufficient for the day, perhaps a quarter of a loaf of bread and something to go with it. I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, I'd like to know whether anyone from the Zvornik Brigade came to Orahovac that day with a vehicle to bring your food or juices or stuff like that? Did that happen during that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I don't remember that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another issue, always dealing with Orahovac. And -- or maybe I will -- I will ask you a few questions about your -- the military police battalion. You can confirm that the military police battalion was divided into platoons as well as into sections; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: It was a military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's my mistake, I'm sorry. So the military police company was -- you had some sections in the military police company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That is correct. Each company has platoons and sections or squads.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And each of those platoons or squads usually there is a platoon commander or a squad leader or a squad commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. There were platoon commanders, but in war you would appoint a section or squad commanders per assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So when you -- you had those platoon commanders and then the squad commanders, they're appointed on the need for each different assignment. Now, you also have, and correct me if I'm wrong, but you also have the company has a second in command also; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: The second along the chain of command. This was assigned by the company commander when he was not present. He would appoint somebody to continue the chain of command, to be in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to go over with you the organisation of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I think we'll go into private session for this, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Technical difficulties. Okay. We got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. We are back in public session now. Now, when you are -- what you said at page 21, lines 13 to 14, is that when you saw Drago Nikolic along with the tall officer, they -- according to your recollection, they were on the road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I think that that was on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And at page 19, line 17, you confirmed that for you there is no doubt that this officer is not from the Zvornik Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: That's correct. Not from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also mentioned at page 21, lines 3 to 5, that although you don't know the exact time when you saw this conversation, it happened in early afternoon, to the best of your recollection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours. I can't say exactly when. It wasn't early in the morning, it wasn't late at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And at page 21, lines 22 to 23, you mentioned that the prisoners at that time were in the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now I get to my two questions concerning this conversation. The first one is quite simple: You did not hear that conversation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And my second question is that looking at the conversation from where you were I am suggesting to you that at that time Drago Nikolic was speaking to the tall officer who was somebody who was higher in rank than he was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Most likely, yes, since I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move to the part where you mentioned that -- seeing Drago Nikolic moving around in his car, and that was on page 23, lines 11 to 13. Do you recall testifying to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this I would just like to come back to also something you said and that is that the -- a question was posed to you whether there were escorts following the vehicles to the site where the people apparently were killed. And you answered on page 22, line 20 to 22, that you don't know if there were escorts following those vehicles to that site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now -- sorry, I apologise. There are many reasons -- you will agree with me there are many reasons why you cannot recall this? First one would be it is one of those details you just can't recall. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And another reason could be that where you were, and you referred to that in your response on page 22, because of where you were you could not really see if any cars were following or any escorts were following these trucks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you are also able to confirm that at some parts of the day during your stay in Orahovac you were at different places around the school and at one point you were actually posted behind the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if I say that when those trucks are taking the prisoners to another site, that during that period which lasted quite a bit of time, according to your testimony, you were not always close to the door where they are being taken out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I wasn't there at all times. I was there sometimes and sometimes I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that's one of the reasons why, another reason why today you cannot say whether these trucks were being escorted to that site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Correct. I even said that for a while I slept, which means that I was in the same place. I was able to see some things, I wasn't able to see other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, this one I need to come back to, because I -- the way I understood it, when you slept that wasn't at the same time that the prisoners were taken out, but I may be wrong. Can you tell us that maybe part of the time when the trucks are taking the prisoners to the site, part of that time you were sleeping. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: I think that I slept prior to that, because I was there the whole time. I don't remember when I went to bed, when I fell asleep, when I got up, at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you don't exclude the possibility that you were sleeping during part of the time that the trucks are being taken -- that the trucks are taking the prisoners to the other site. That's a possibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-143
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a truck left earlier, I can't tell you what happened while I was sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about put them marked for identification for the moment, and I would like to ask Mr. Nicholls to come back as soon as possible, then we can sort it -- sort them out. Would you agree, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's acceptable, but it's just that I think you will find we didn't cherry pick; we put all the documents in. We actually didn't even have time to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Those three exhibits will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, I will come back very quickly. I don't think I will have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I was told, informed by the deputy -- court deputy, that 1692 was already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You are correct. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I was told that -- we have only 10 minutes, and the next witness for some private reasons, he returned to the hotel, which I allowed. So -- so that's the hearing for today. And any preliminaries? Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That concludes the hearing for today. Tomorrow the hearing will be in the afternoon. 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 31st day of January, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
